privacy_promise: Your logs stay on this phone. We never send raw tracking logs over the network.
consult_doctor: Consider consulting a doctor for personalized medical guidance.

flag_cycle_length_anomaly.title: Cycle Length Variation
flag_cycle_length_anomaly.explanation: Your recent cycle length differs noticeably from your personal historical baseline range.
contributing_signals: Cycle length increased by > 5 days compared to baseline
flag_cycle_length_anomaly.recommendation: If this pattern persists over 2-3 cycles, consider consulting a doctor.

flag_pain_spike.title: Pain Score Elevation
flag_pain_spike.explanation: Pain severity scores logged over consecutive days are higher than your usual baseline average.
contributing_signals: Pain score level 7-10 logged for 2+ consecutive days
flag_pain_spike.recommendation: Track accompanying symptoms closely and consider consulting a doctor if pain is unmanageable.

flag_flow_change.title: Flow Volume Pattern Shift
flag_flow_change.explanation: Flow intensity logs show a sudden change relative to your historical cycle pattern.
contributing_signals: Heavy flow logged on non-peak days
Abrupt transition from light to heavy flow
flag_flow_change.recommendation: Ensure adequate hydration and iron intake. Consider consulting a doctor if heavy flow persists.

flag_irregular_pattern.title: Irregular Baseline Rhythm
flag_irregular_pattern.explanation: Cycle intervals display high variability compared to your expected variance band.
contributing_signals: Standard deviation of cycle length exceeds 6 days
Interval spacing varies month to month
flag_irregular_pattern.recommendation: Keep logging to strengthen your baseline statistics. Consider consulting a doctor if cycles stay unpredictable.

myths.title: Myth: Cold food causes severe menstrual cramps
myths.transcript: Fact: Cramps are caused by muscle contractions in the uterus driven by prostaglandins, not by drinking cold water or eating cold food. Warm comfort foods can help relax muscles, but temperature alone does not cause cramping.

myths.title: Myth: Irregular cycles always mean fertility problems
myths.transcript: Fact: Minor cycle variations are common due to stress, sleep changes, diet, or illness. Screening patterns help track trends over time. Consider consulting a doctor if irregularity persists.
